projects.name: Procurement of health products for diagnostics and treatment of noncommunicable diseases (NCD)
projects.description:
The Government of Turkmenistan is strongly committed to protecting health of the people. Control of noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) and reducing their economic burden is a top priority on the national development agenda. Since 2021, the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry of Turkmenistan and UNDP implemented two NCD projects with total budget of more than $92 mln. Implementation of the joint projects ensured availability of high quality, affordable and free-of-charge medicines for treatment of major NCD and rare diseases, maternal and neonatal health, as well provided technical assistance and capacitating health workforce for management of NCDs, and overall strengthening of the national health system. 
Based on the successful implementation of the NCD projects and to ensure continuous provision of the quality health services and achieve long-term impact, MOHMI and UNDP initiated a new 2-year project on strengthening integrated health services on lab diagnostics and treatment of the NCD, rare diseases, maternal and neonatal health, with focus on primary health care facilities.
The overall aim of the project will be to improve health outcomes for NCDs, rare diseases, maternal and neonatal emergencies, through improving access to equitable, quality and affordable essential health services for all.

projects.name: Procurement for clinical laboratory services in Turkmenistan
projects.description:
The Government of Turkmenistan is strongly committed to protecting health of the people. Since 2023, the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry of Turkmenistan (MOHMI) and UNDP have been implementing a project to strengthen laboratory services for the diagnosis of various diseases, with a budget of 18 million USD. As part of the laboratory project, 121 laboratories across the country have been modernized to deliver the essential clinical analyses. 
Referring to the successful implementation of a project, the MOHMI and UNDP have initiated a new two-year project for ensuring the sustainable provision of high-quality medical services, achieve a long-term impact of the project and further strengthening of the laboratory diagnostic of diseases, with a focus on primary healthcare facilities. 

The goal of the project “Strengthening clinical laboratory services in Turkmenistan in 2026-2027” is to strengthen the potential of national healthcare system in the field of clinical laboratory diagnostic of diseases. 

The project will support healthcare services to ensure the availability, accessibility, reliability and modern laboratory analyses for accurate and timely diagnosis of the most common illnesses, including infectious and noncommunicable diseases, surgery, emergency, maternal and child healthcare and others. The project will focus on laboratory capacity in primary healthcare facilities, but will also support secondary and tertiary care facilities.

projects.name: Infection control and waste management
projects.description:
Infection control and waste management are critical components in UNDP-supported health projects in Turkmenistan, as they directly safeguard patient safety, protect healthcare workers, and prevent the spread of infections within and beyond healthcare facilities. In projects focused on procurement of essential medicines for non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, tuberculosis, HIV, viral hepatitis and other infectious diseases as well as in laboratory strengthening, these measures minimize the risk of healthcare-associated infections, particularly in settings treating chronic and drug-resistant conditions where patients may have prolonged hospital stays or compromised immunity. Effective infection prevention protocols, including the provision of personal protective equipment (PPE), biosafety equipment, and ventilation systems, combined with rigorous waste management practices, reduce cross-transmission of pathogens, prevent amplification of antimicrobial resistance, and maintain the integrity of treatment outcomes.
Proper waste management — encompassing safe segregation, collection, decontamination (e.g., through units such as Sterilwave SW100 and Medister 160), and environmentally sound disposal of infectious, sharp, pharmaceutical, and chemical waste — eliminates secondary hazards to the community and the environment. These activities ensure compliance with international biosafety standards, protect vulnerable populations (including remote residents and low-income households), and support the sustainability of health system investments during the transition to full domestic funding. By mitigating occupational and environmental risks, infection control and waste management contribute to the overall resilience, equity, and long-term effectiveness of national health programmes in alignment with SDG 3 targets.

projects.description:
Strengthening the capacity of Turkmenistan to comply with the ETF under the Paris Agreement.
The Paris Agreement, adopted at COP 21 in December 2015 and entering into force in November 2016, established a global framework requiring all Parties to implement robust measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) systems to transparently communicate climate actions and support. In line with these obligations, the Global Environment Facility (GEF) approved on 18 October 2023 a Project Identification Form and Project Preparation Grant submitted by FAO for the project “Strengthening the capacity of Turkmenistan to comply with the Enhanced Transparency Framework under the Paris Agreement.” Funded under the CBIT program and GEF-8, and implemented by FAO with the Interstate Commission on Sustainable Development as executing partner, the project aims to strengthen Turkmenistan’s national capacities to meet Enhanced Transparency Framework requirements for tracking climate change mitigation and adaptation actions, as well as support received, particularly in sectors covered by the country’s nationally determined contributions.

projects.name: Adherence support of MDR-TB patients
projects.description:
By the end of 2027, the National Tuberculosis Programme of Turkmenistan plans to complete a full transition to domestic funding and exit from Global Fund support. 
In this context, adherence support for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) patients remains significantly important. MDR-TB treatment involves prolonged regimens (often 9–24 months) with second-line drugs that frequently cause severe adverse effects, leading to high risks of treatment interruption or default. Incomplete adherence is the primary cause of further drug resistance, including progression to extensively drug-resistant TB (XDR-TB), which carries substantially worse outcomes and higher costs. Sustained high treatment success rates — particularly for MDR-TB — are therefore essential to protect the epidemiological gains already achieved (low mortality and declining incidence) and to ensure the long-term sustainability of the national TB response under full domestic financing.

projects.name: Technical assistance (capacity building of health specialists, updating national protocols and technical assistance of international experts) including through WHO and UNFPA
projects.description:
Technical assistance, encompassing capacity building of health specialists, updating of national protocols, and engagement of international experts (particularly through WHO and UNFPA), is of paramount importance in UNDP-supported health projects in Turkmenistan for several fundamental reasons.
First, it ensures the adoption of evidence-based, internationally aligned clinical practices in a context where drug-resistant tuberculosis, non-communicable diseases, and other priority health conditions require precise, standardized, and high-quality management. Continuous training of healthcare professionals — delivered by WHO experts — equips clinicians with up-to-date knowledge on diagnostics, treatment regimens (including shorter DR-TB regimens), adverse effect monitoring, and patient-centered care, thereby directly improving treatment success rates and reducing morbidity and mortality. Second, systematic updating of national treatment protocols, guided by WHO recommendations and UNFPA technical input on maternal and child health, guarantees that clinical decision-making reflects the latest global standards, enhances treatment efficacy, minimizes risks of resistance amplification, and promotes rational use of medicines — all essential for long-term epidemiological control and cost-effectiveness. Third, the involvement of international experts provides objective, specialized guidance during critical phases of programme design, implementation, and transition to domestic funding, strengthening national ownership while bridging technical gaps.

projects.name: Strengthening Integrated Water Management in Amu Darya, Zarafshon and Panj River Basins
projects.description:
Strengthening Integrated Water Management in Amu Darya, Zarafshon and Panj River Basins.
The Amu Darya Basin Child Project (ADB-CP), under the Central Asia Water and Land Nexus (CAWLN) Program, seeks to tackle mounting environmental degradation and socio‑economic vulnerabilities in the Amu Darya River Basin by addressing systemic imbalances in water and land use caused by weak coordination, fragmented institutions, data gaps, limited stakeholder engagement, and unsustainable practices. Guided by Integrated Watershed Management, the project promotes a coordinated and resilient approach to managing the Water‑Land Nexus through strengthened transboundary cooperation, improved basin‑wide monitoring, and national‑level actions aligned with regional objectives. Implemented across Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan, the ADB‑CP responds to upstream‑downstream dynamics and builds on each country’s policy commitments, ensuring coherence with national development goals while collectively addressing shared environmental and climate risks in the basin.

By aligning mitigation and adaptation priorities with national development strategies and applying gender‑responsive, inclusive approaches, the project aims to enable effective climate action, attract investment, and support sustainable, resilient development in Turkmenistan.

projects.name: Knowledge of national institutions is strengthened to improve their capacities to respond to climate change impact on cryosphere and related water systems
projects.description: The headwaters of the main river systems in Central Asia heavily depend on the seasonal melting of the cryosphere, with little additional precipitation input in their lower reaches. These rivers sustain the lives and livelihoods of people and support economic development across the region, including in Turkmenistan. However, glaciers in Central Asia are experiencing a rapid loss of mass. Changes in glacier extent and volume will have significant impacts on associated water systems and on the large populations that depend on them. It is therefore essential to understand the impacts of climate change on the cryosphere in Central Asia. The project aims to foster regional cooperation on adaptation strategies, validated through scientific assessments of snow, glaciers, permafrost, and available water resources.

projects.name: Improving adaptive capacity and resilience of local communities to climate change induced water shortages and land degradation in two climate affected regions of Turkmenistan
projects.description: Turkmenistan with its highly arid climate and scarce water resources is particularly vulnerable to the adverse impacts of climate change. The adverse effects of climate change, such as water shortages and land degradation, contribute to economic decline and job loss in the agricultural sector, serving as a push factor of migration from the primary sector dependent regions of Turkmenistan, mainly Dashoguz and Lebap. In these regions, land degradation and shortage of irrigation water for agriculture affect agricultural productivity and, accordingly, quality of life of the local communities, forcing them to migrate. However, for some vulnerable groups, primarily families of migrants left behind and women-led households, migration is not an option because they do not have economic and other resources. In this regard, the project will prioritize adaptation in-situ to build resilience of these vulnerable groups and promote their climate resilient development through demonstration of the efficient use of water resources, use of innovative “green” technologies in land and water use, water-smart practices for greater access to safe drinking water and irrigation, raising public awareness to encourage responsible water consumption, promoting stakeholder interaction and cooperation for better adaptation planning at the local level, and enhancing the knowledge and capacity of targeted vulnerable groups as well as local administrations through education and training.

projects.description:
The project will provide technical and institutional support to the Ministry of Agriculture and its Land Resources Service to reform and upgrade its national crop monitoring systems using remote sensing technology. 
The project aims to strengthen Turkmenistan’s crop monitoring system by introducing remote sensing technologies to improve efficiency, accuracy, and reliability, while ensuring long-term sustainability through institutional capacity building. Implemented collaboratively with the Ministry of Agriculture, related institutions, academia, civil society, and the private sector, the project will be guided by a Project Steering Committee and supported by a Technical Working Group. Through FAO-led technical assistance under the TCP, stakeholders will gain advanced skills in remote sensing, GIS, land use monitoring, and improved business processes for crop forecasting and reporting, with practical testing at pilot sites. A comprehensive training and lifelong learning program, including integration into university curricula, will support lasting knowledge transfer. By enabling early detection of crop stress, precision agriculture, and evidence-based policy-making, the project will enhance agricultural productivity, resilience, and sustainability, with findings and policy recommendations widely disseminated to ensure broad ownership and long-term impact.

At the policy level, the project will raise awareness among decision-makers and provide technical recommendations to integrate sustainable soil management into national agricultural strategies. projects.name: Digital solutions in health services
projects.description:
Digital solutions in health projects play a pivotal role in improving access, adherence, and overall management of health services in Turkmenistan.
In these initiatives, a bilingual mobile application has been developed and deployed to enable registered patients to view their prescribed medicines, access detailed treatment information, and better adhere to therapy regimens. Concurrently, digital warehouse management systems have been introduced to facilitate real-time monitoring of medicine distribution, storage conditions, expiration dates, and rational dispensing practices across all levels of the health system. For tuberculosis control efforts, piloting of advanced digital adherence tools includes Video Supported Treatment (VST) and smart pillboxes, while the rollout of an electronic TB register (TB-RRIS) has commenced to enhance case management, surveillance, and reporting accuracy. These digital innovations reduce geographic and logistical barriers, strengthen patient-centered care, minimize treatment interruptions, support evidence-based decision-making, and contribute to more efficient and sustainable health service delivery as the country advances toward full domestic funding and self-reliance. Additionally, in Turkmenistan, CAD4TB has been implemented through UNDP-led initiatives supported by the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria. As of late 2025, portable X-ray units equipped with CAD4TB are deployed to expand TB screening, particularly in remote areas, by bringing diagnostic services directly to communities. Artificial intelligence rapidly analyzes images for TB signs, enabling timely detection and reducing barriers such as travel to centralized facilities. National medical personnel receive comprehensive training to maximize effectiveness, aligning with WHO recommendations for AI-assisted screening in adults and contributing to strengthened national TB control efforts. This technology transforms traditional screening into a mobile, efficient, and accessible process, supporting early diagnosis and program scalability in the transition toward domestic funding.

- Responds to the country’s population dynamics (age structure, fertility, mortality, migration, urbanization, etc.) and megatrends (climate change, digitalization, economic transformation, and labor shifts).
- Provides strategic policy directions, promotes legal frameworks, and identifies programmatic interventions aimed at maximizing the demographic dividend and promoting human capital development.

framework.name: Good Governance and Inclusive and Diversified Economic Growth

children.name: By 2030, the people of Turkmenistan have access to accountable governance system through improved public administration and strengthened fiscal capacity, based on commitments to human rights, rule of law and gender equality
The public administration plans and manages sustainable development in a transparent, participatory, efficient and coordinated manner, using digital solutions and adequate budgetary resources
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
•	Strengthening institutional capacity for sustainable (socially, economically, demographically, and spatially) development planning and budgeting with a LNOB approach
•	Introducing digital technologies, improving the digital infrastructure of public institutions and increasing the level of digital literacy among civil servants 
•	Supporting mechanisms for intergovernmental cooperation and coordination with development partners to monitor the implementation and achievement of the SDGs 
•	Strengthening national capacities to make better use of the demographic dividend and to formulate development policies and plans that take into account spatial localisation
•	Supporting the implementation of the National Anti-Corruption Programme 2025-2029

children.name: Disaggregated and reliable data is available to inform policymaking and monitor progress towards the SDGs
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
●	Improving statistical information management systems to collect reliable disaggregated data on SDG targets and indicators, including strengthening the statistical capacity of governmental organisations
●	Developing national monitoring and evaluation mechanisms and capacities for results-based policies and programmes, including the adequacy, effectiveness and equity of social investments for SDG implementation

children.name: The government's national policy and legal framework are consistent with international commitments on human rights, rule of law, access to justice and gender equality and is supported by implementation mechanisms and strengthened institutional capacity
children.description:
Indicative areas of work: 
●	Improving the judicial system based on international standards and recommendations of the UPR, UN treaty bodies and ILO supervisory bodies, including procedures to ensure access to justice for minors
●	 Improving protection systems and procedures for providing free legal aid to vulnerable groups (expanding the possibilities for providing such services);
●	 Improving legislation in providing services and protecting women from all forms of violence.
●	Strengthening the capacity of national agencies to systematically address the most pending human rights issues, including violence against women and protection of reproductive rights; protection of children's rights, including from violence; ensuring migrants' rights; combating human trafficking, forced and child labour, etc.
●	Strengthening the capacity of law enforcement and judicial authorities to prevent and combat transnational organised crime, torture, drug trafficking and corruption in accordance with international standards and best practices, as well as ensuring access to remedies and protection of victims 
●	Strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ombudsman Office as an independent national human rights institution to promote, protect and realize human rights in accordance with the Paris Principles 
●	Maintaining a tripartite systematic dialogue and partnership with civil society on projects and initiatives aimed at developing equitable and inclusive societies 
●	Strengthening the national electoral system in line with international standards

children.name: By 2030, Turkmenistan will have improved conditions and opportunities for inclusive and sustainable economic diversification and growth
Turkmenistan better integrated into regional and global trade networks
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
●	Strengthening the capacity of Turkmenistan's political participation in the WTO accession process and the capacity of government institutions in trade facilitation reforms. 
●	Introducing trade facilitation practices. Modernising market infrastructure in the agricultural sector, storage facilities, logistics to reduce food losses, increase competitiveness of Turkmen business through certification and simplification of trade procedures.
●	Improving the ecosystem for investment promotion and e-commerce, including banking services
●	Improving the regulatory framework for securities market development to facilitate investment 
●	Expanding energy links and development of electricity trade 
●	Improving trade and transport links and logistics 
●	Improving and further digitalising customs services, including a Single Window for export and import customs clearance 
●	Digitalization of multimodal data and document exchange for digital trade and transport corridors crossing Turkmenistan

children.name: The business climate in Turkmenistan supports structural transformation of the economy, growth and increased competitiveness of the private sector
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
●	Enhancing the national capacity in the area of industrial and innovation policies and development of government measures to restructure and diversify the economy and enhance research and development
●	Integrating SMEs into sustainable value chains. Enhancing capacity of business support organisations to provide quality services to SMEs. Increased access to finance, including for women-led and rural businesses. Developing a start-up ecosystem and increased access to innovation, innovation adoption, digitalisation of data and document exchange in supply chains 
●	Supporting sectoral restructuring and enhancing private sector quality assurance and competitiveness in the production, processing and manufacturing sectors 
●	Improving the legislative framework for public-private partnership 
●	Maintaining a sustainable dialogue with the private sector

children.name: Formal, decent and safe employment and livelihood opportunities increased and working conditions improved in sectors of the economy with high employment potential, including among women, youth, people with disabilities and returning migrants in vulnerable situation
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
●	Improvement of the system of recruitment, job selection and formalisation of employment through an effective system of labour market regulation, monitoring and forecasting of the labour market. Development and implementation of a road map for the development of the labour market of Turkmenistan until 2030
●	Strengthening the capacity of public institutions to design and implement active labour market strategies and innovative programmes, developing soft and digital skills for the employment of people from rural communities, people with disabilities, youth, women, returning migrants in vulnerable situation and other vulnerable groups of population
●	Improving the ability smallholder farmers to access support services and financial resources 
●	Improvement of the employment services system, empowerment of labour inspectorates in line with fundamental principles in the field of labour, especially in sectors with intensive employment
●	Supporting the development of World Heritage management capacities by enhancing and improving the working conditions of heritage professionals.

framework.name: Environment and Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation

children.name: By 2030, Turkmenistan will strengthen natural resource management systems, systematically fulfil its climate change commitments, and the population will become more resilient to climate change and disasters
Climate change adaptation and mitigation measures are implemented in accordance with the Paris Agreement
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
▪	Alignment of national policies and institutional frameworks with international conventions and agreements. Strengthening the capacity of governments to fulfil international environmental commitments
▪	Supporting the introduction of budgetary financing mechanisms in the field of climate and environment 
▪	Integrating the concept of integrated water resources management and energy efficiency into policy and practice 
▪	Supporting the implementation of the global commitment to reduce methane and other GHG emissions 
▪	Improving methods of sustainable agricultural development 
▪	Incorporating climate change issues into formal education at all levels, from preschool to tertiary level  
▪	Introducing and expanding the Green Schools programme, which promotes green skills among children and youth. Active involvement of young people in the climate change agenda 
▪	Strengthening health system resilience to climate change to address health risks and impacts. 
▪	Adopting sustainable practices and measures for climate change mitigation and adaptation for vulnerable populations  
▪	Improving sustainable urban and territorial planning and development to reduce carbon emissions. Integrating NDC and NAP priorities into national urbanisation policies
▪	Application of UNECE environmental conventions in Turkmenistan
▪	Designing and implementing climate-resilient public infrastructure, including health, education, and water facilities.
▪	Supporting infrastructure-based solutions for methane capture and reduction in agriculture and waste management sectors.

children.name: National climate early warning and DRR systems are aligned with the Sendai Framework for DRR and their capacities are strengthened
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
▪	Strengthening national capacities in early warning and DRR, modernising related infrastructure and introducing technologies  
▪	Improving emergency preparedness and response capacity of relevant government agencies and non-governmental sector partners 
▪	Integrating emergency preparedness and resilience to all types of emergencies (including gender-based violence and human trafficking) into health, education, social protection and information systems, including prevention and response, ensuring continuity
▪	Supporting the National Action Plan to strengthen a social protection system capable of responding to emergencies. Strengthening the capacity of the health system and other relevant government agencies, including at border crossings to prevent, rapidly detect and effectively respond to all health emergencies
▪	Building resilience to climate change by strengthening people-centred, gender-sensitive and climate risk-sensitive knowledge base and capacities
▪	Improving sustainable urban and territorial planning and development to reduce risks and enhance resilience

children.name: Circularity and resource efficiency concepts are mainstreamed into policy and practice
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
▪	Developing and adopting policies, programmes and regulations that promote "green" norms of social behaviour, including circularity and waste management. Shaping these norms through public awareness and formal education 
▪	Developing and adopting policies, regulations and programmes to support the transition to low-carbon development policies, renewable energy and green economy linkages, including the green energy transition 
▪	Assessing the policy, technology and financing situation for the green energy transition. Capacity building of technical experts and decision makers at all levels to develop and implement policies 
▪	Demonstrating approaches to rational use of land, water, forest and other natural resources
▪	Designing, constructing, and operationalizing green infrastructure
▪	Strengthening protected area management and biodiversity conservation through field-level interventions, such as eco-sensitive infrastructure, environmental monitoring systems, capacity building and ecotourism models that balance conservation and livelihoods.
▪	Implementation of effective methods for the management of protected areas and conservation of biodiversity

children.name: By 2030, all people of Turkmenistan, including vulnerable groups, benefit equitably from quality and inclusive health, education and social protection systems and transformative social norms
Health policies,  financing, institutional and human capacities strengthened to ensure universal access to quality health services for all
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
▪	Developing and implementing public health policies and programmes, and financing efficiency approaches to improve the quality of health services. Integrating essential social services into national urbanisation policies 
▪	Strengthening people-centred primary health care, including equitable access to quality health, products, medicines and vaccines, capacity of health workers, collection and analysis of health data 
▪	Strengthening maternal and child health, reproductive health and family planning services. Improving infant and young child nutrition, including breastfeeding and complementary feeding, early detection and intervention services. Integrating reproductive health into education systems in schools and beyond, including digital spaces. 
▪	Developing a digital health system 
▪	Implementing a ICD-11 implementation  roadmap and the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) in the health care system.  Reforming of medical and social expert assessment (regulatory framework, directions, data management, piloting) in accordance with the ICF 
▪	Strengthening the health system to combat NCDs (CVDs, diabetes, cancer, COPD and mental health) through prevention, screening, treatment, rehabilitation, palliative care and control of NCD risk factors 
▪	Strengthening the capacity of MHPSS frontline workers and developing services for young people and families
▪	Strengthening the health system to combat communicable diseases, including tuberculosis, hepatitis, HIV/AIDS and STIs, influenza, zoonoses 
▪	Strengthening the national programme for immunisation and control of VPI with focus on polio and acute flaccid paralysis, measles and rubella surveillance, including supply chain innovations
▪	Strengthening national capacities to implement the One Health approach
▪	Strengthening national capacities for risk prevention and reduction, strategic and operational preparedness and resilience, and effective response to health emergencies and those caused by all hazards, including pandemics
▪	Introducing behavioural and cultural approaches to improve health literacy, promote healthy lifestyles. Improving the nutrition of the entire population, including women of reproductive age and adolescent girls. Increasing public awareness of healthy diets, food and nutrition security and the gradual transition of production, distribution, retailing and consumption to more sustainable and resilient agri-food systems. 
▪	Promoting and supporting positive parenting through information, counselling, guidance and behavioural modelling, including through demonstration and practical sessions

children.name: The education system, from pre-primary to tertiary, provides quality, inclusive and safe learning opportunities for all children and young people, including children with disabilities
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
●	Implementing a strategy to increase access to preschool education and early childhood development opportunities, including the diversification of preschool education by introducing a one-year half-day quality preschool education programme. 
●	Supporting the role of parents in early childhood development: Empowering and supporting parents to create rich learning and developmental experiences for children 
●	Implementing an inclusive education policy for children with disabilities in line with the national concept of inclusive education. Supporting the inclusion of children with disabilities in mainstream schools. Reform of the Medical and Pedagogical Commissions under the Ministry of Education in line with the ICF and CRPD (normative framework, orientations, data management, piloting) to support inclusive education and de-institutionalisation 
●	Strengthening educational (rehabilitation) centres under the Ministry of Education as resource centres to support inclusive education and intersectoral services for people with disabilities (transdisciplinary and interdisciplinary support, augmentative and alternative communication).
●	Introducing gender-sensitive and inclusive standards for safe learning spaces for children, covering prevention, response and victim support
●	Improving the mechanism for providing social services to vulnerable groups, including patients with TB and other infectious diseases.
●	Increased life skills training opportunities for young people, including positive masculinity norms for young men

children.name: Increased coverage and sustainability of social protection programmes, and scaled up inclusive and quality community-based social services to meet the needs of vulnerable groups and protect them from all forms of violence
children.description:
Indicative areas of work:
▪	Improving the legal and regulatory framework and reduction of barriers (geographical, financial, social) for access to quality social services 
▪	Improving the legal and regulatory framework, as well as specific policies related to the national child protection system strengthening
▪	Strengthening capacity for effective implementation of social assistance programmes among national and local organizations
▪	Strengthening the child protection governance structures, including coordination across government departments, between levels of decentralization and between formal and informal actors     
▪	Implementing structural changes in the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection of the Population to roll out social protection services across the country, establishment of social protection directorates and departments in velayats and etraps. Expanding community-based social services and specialised services along with capacity building of social work specialists in each etrap.
▪	Strengthening the capacity of psychosocial support professionals and developing community-based services for young people 
▪	Strengthening rehabilitation centres under the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry as inclusive resource centres for cross-sectoral inclusive services for persons with disabilities (rehabilitation and habilitation, early intervention, inclusive education) in line with the ICF and CRPD. Promoting a multi-sectoral system of assistive technologies and products for people with disabilities as part of the national rehabilitation strategy 
▪	Introducing and expanding specialised support services for families with children, including reintegration services for families with children with disabilities and in difficult life situations 
▪	Increasing institutional capacity and improved referral systems and services to protect women and children from all forms of violence. Introducing a system of special services for child protection and prevention of child violence. Supporting systems to challenge social norms to achieve gender equality and eliminate all forms of gender-based violence 
▪	Strengthening a range of services and programmes available that prevent unnecessary separation from the family, including gatekeeping by competent authorities, awareness of the harms of institutionalisation of children, and family support services aimed at preventing separation
▪	Strengthening systems of reintegration support for returning migrants in vulnerable situations and their families through a case management approach across economic, social and psychological dimensions, taking into account their specific needs, vulnerability, age, gender as well as skills, knowledge and transnational networks they acquired in migration.
▪	Developing new social protection packages for different type disabilities (cash plus services) based on the additional costs associated with disability
▪	Strengthening inter-sectoral coordination and referral mechanisms to provide integrated services to vulnerable population groups
